items.answer: Hundreds of thousands of Kosovo Albanians fled into neighbouring states, threatening regional stability and reaching Western Europe. Refugee flows into Europe gave Western states a direct interest in Kosovo, absent in Rwanda.
items.markingKey: Context (Hundreds of thousands of Kosovo Albanians fled into neighbouring states, threatening regional stability and reaching Western Europe.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Refugee flows into Europe gave Western states a direct interest in Kosovo, absent in Rwanda. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to the role of interests in shaping intervention.

items.stem: Analyse one strength and one limitation of the view that NATO’s intervention in Kosovo in 1999 was motivated primarily by humanitarian concerns.
items.answer: Humanitarian concerns were real and important, but intervention also served NATO’s credibility and European security interests.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: ethnic cleansing and memory of Srebrenica (1995); Blair’s doctrine of the international community; refugee crisis. Arguments against: NATO credibility at its 50th anniversary; regional stability and refugee flows into Europe; US strategic interest in the Balkans. Supported judgement: Humanitarian concerns were real and important, but intervention also served NATO’s credibility and European security interests.

items.stem: To what extent is it true that the international administration of Kosovo between 1999 and 2008 was a failure?
items.answer: It prevented renewed war and built institutions but failed to protect minorities or resolve status.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: failed to protect minorities (2004 riots); divided Mitrovica; slow economic development and corruption. Arguments against: maintained peace between Serbia and Kosovo; built institutions and held elections from 2001; refugee return of Albanians. Supported judgement: It prevented renewed war and built institutions but failed to protect minorities or resolve status. items.stem: Evaluate the claim that Kosovo’s declaration of independence in 2008 resolved the Kosovo question.
items.answer: Independence changed Kosovo’s status in practice but did not settle the question internationally.
items.markingKey: Arguments for: ICJ opinion 2010; over 100 recognitions; state institutions and constitution. Arguments against: Serbia, Russia, China and five EU states do not recognise it; north Kosovo resists Pristina; no UN membership; tensions continue. Supported judgement: Independence changed Kosovo’s status in practice but did not settle the question internationally. items.stem: Which of the following best describes "humanitarian intervention"?
options: The use of military force by states in another state, without its consent, to prevent or end mass atrocities
A court in The Hague, established in 2015–2016 under Kosovo law, to try alleged crimes by KLA members
The Bosnian town where Bosnian Serb forces killed about 8,000 Bosniak men and boys in July 1995, despite the presence of Dutch UN peacekeepers
The principle, developed by the ICISS in 2001 and endorsed at the UN World Summit in 2005, that states must protect populations from atrocities and the international community may act if they fail
items.answer: The use of military force by states in another state, without its consent, to prevent or end mass atrocities
items.markingKey: A. "humanitarian intervention" is the use of military force by states in another state, without its consent, to prevent or end mass atrocities.

items.stem: Which term matches this description: "The UN Security Council resolution of 10 June 1999 that placed Kosovo under UN interim administration with an international security presence"?
items.answer: Resolution 1244
items.markingKey: C. This is the definition of Resolution 1244.

items.stem: Explain the difference between the Kosovo Specialist Chambers and the ICTY.
items.answer: The ICTY was a UN tribunal (1993–2017) trying crimes across the former Yugoslavia, mostly by Serb leaders in the Kosovo cases; the Specialist Chambers is a Kosovo court sitting in The Hague to try crimes by KLA members.
items.markingKey: The ICTY was a UN tribunal (1993–2017) trying crimes across the former Yugoslavia, mostly by Serb leaders in the Kosovo cases; the Specialist Chambers is a Kosovo court sitting in The Hague to try crimes by KLA members. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Distinguish between the international response in Rwanda and the international response in Kosovo.
items.answer: In Rwanda the UN reduced its force and major powers refused to intervene during the genocide; in Kosovo NATO used force within months of the main atrocities, without UN authorisation.
items.markingKey: In Rwanda the UN reduced its force and major powers refused to intervene during the genocide; in Kosovo NATO used force within months of the main atrocities, without UN authorisation. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Explain the difference between its legitimacy and the legality of the Kosovo intervention.
items.answer: Legality concerns conformity with international law (UN Charter); legitimacy concerns moral justification. The Kosovo Commission judged it illegal but legitimate.
items.markingKey: Legality concerns conformity with international law (UN Charter); legitimacy concerns moral justification. The Kosovo Commission judged it illegal but legitimate. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Explain why minorities in Kosovo were at risk after June 1999.
items.answer: Returning Albanians took revenge on Serbs and Roma accused of collaboration; KFOR could not protect scattered communities, and about 200,000 non-Albanians left.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Returning Albanians took revenge on Serbs and Roma accused of collaboration; KFOR could not protect scattered communities, and about 200,000 non-Albanians left. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Rafael writes: "The ICTY prosecuted only Serbs for crimes in Kosovo." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: It also tried KLA commanders such as Ramush Haradinaj and Fatmir Limaj, who were acquitted, which fuelled controversy about witness intimidation.
items.markingKey: It also tried KLA commanders such as Ramush Haradinaj and Fatmir Limaj, who were acquitted, which fuelled controversy about witness intimidation. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Mei writes: "The international community intervened in Kosovo because more people were killed there than in Rwanda." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Far more were killed in Rwanda; Kosovo’s location in Europe, NATO credibility and refugee flows explain the different response.
items.markingKey: Far more were killed in Rwanda; Kosovo’s location in Europe, NATO credibility and refugee flows explain the different response. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem:
Source B: Independent International Commission on Kosovo (chaired by Richard Goldstone), The Kosovo Report, Oxford University Press, 2000 (adapted)

The NATO military intervention was illegal but legitimate. It was illegal because it did not receive prior approval from the UN Security Council. However, it was justified because all diplomatic avenues had been exhausted and it liberated the majority population of Kosovo from a long period of oppression.

What does Source B suggest about Operation Allied Force and the debate on humanitarian intervention? Refer closely to the source in your answer.
items.answer: NATO’s action broke international law but was morally justified because diplomacy had failed and it ended oppression.
items.markingKey: NATO’s action broke international law but was morally justified because diplomacy had failed and it ended oppression. Award 1 mark for each relevant point drawn from the source, up to [3]. Points must come from the source itself; own knowledge is not credited in this question.

items.stem: With reference to the divided city of Mitrovica, explain how it illustrates the limits of international administration.
items.answer: The Ibar river separated an Albanian south from a Serb-majority north that remained linked to Belgrade’s parallel structures. UNMIK could not integrate the north, which remained a flashpoint and challenge to Kosovo’s sovereignty.
items.markingKey: Context (The Ibar river separated an Albanian south from a Serb-majority north that remained linked to Belgrade’s parallel structures.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: UNMIK could not integrate the north, which remained a flashpoint and challenge to Kosovo’s sovereignty. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to the limits of international administration.

items.stem: Outline one way in which the ICTY judgment in Prosecutor v. Šainović et al. (2009) shows international accountability for crimes in Kosovo.
items.answer: Five senior Serbian and Yugoslav officials were convicted of deportation and murder in Kosovo; Milan Milutinović was acquitted. It established judicially that a campaign of expulsion was carried out by state forces in 1999.
items.markingKey: Context (Five senior Serbian and Yugoslav officials were convicted of deportation and murder in Kosovo; Milan Milutinović was acquitted.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: It established judicially that a campaign of expulsion was carried out by state forces in 1999. – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to international accountability for crimes in Kosovo.

items.stem:
Source C: Paraphrased from Bill Clinton, US President, speech at Kigali airport, 25 March 1998

The international community, Africa included, must bear its share of responsibility for this tragedy. We could have done more to stop what happened in Rwanda. The world must not be indifferent again.

What does Source C suggest about why the international community responded differently in Rwanda and Kosovo? Refer closely to the source in your answer.
items.answer: The international community, including the USA, failed Rwanda and should have done more.

items.stem: To what extent was Operation Allied Force a successful humanitarian intervention?
items.answer: It achieved its main aims but at significant humanitarian and legal cost, so success was partial.
items.markingKey: Indicative content: ended Serbian rule and allowed refugee return; expulsions accelerated during bombing; civilian casualties and legality; reverse ethnic cleansing of Serbs and Roma after June 1999. items.answer: They achieved basic security and institutions but failed to create a stable multi-ethnic society.
